channel.title: The Talas Herald
channel.description: News from Talas and across Irad.

item.title: Kara-Suu Canyon car park and guide fees raise IS 610,000 in nine months
item.description: Sary-Bulak District says Talas families and school parties supplied most of it; clans on the upper canyon's tribal side receive none.

item.title: Kyrgyz state banks drop 284 firms over sanctions risk; Irad, on Kyrgyz paper, counts its exposure
item.description: About 41 more firms are reportedly under review in Bishkek; no Iradi company is named, but the banks that carry Irad's trade have given no figures.

item.title: Donor adds IS 37.8m for clinics and health posts; list of sites not yet published
item.description: The US$4.5 million equals 30 per cent of the IS 126 million the Health Ministry wants for primary care in 2027, and the partner behind it is not named.

item.title: Dealer plans US$3m farm-machinery service centre at Kara-Bulak; loan terms unpublished
item.description: A Talasbank loan of about $2 million and a $1 million Rural Development Fund share would pay for 35 jobs and repair bays by spring sowing.

item.title: Remittance families deserve to see the number between the rates
item.description: Between 5% and 8% of GDP arrives from abroad, and nobody publishes what it costs a family to receive it.

item.title: Two held in Nurzhan over fake Bazar heater and air-filter ads; 14 buyers lost 5,900 som
item.description: Police say advances of 120 to 600 som were sent by card transfer outside the Tulpar app as smog and the heating season set in.

item.title: Remittances from Russia run US$250–400m; families say fees and rate bite
item.description: A dollar paid out at the official 8.40 buys about 27% fewer som than at the Bazar-i Kalan, and the Ministry of Labour announces nothing new.

item.title: Cameras record two snow leopards in upper Besh-Tash; no herder compensation published
item.description: Rangers want night corrals and a call line as herds come down, but the valley is tribal land and the Akjele elders must agree first.

item.title: Uzbek workers abroad halve, remittances quadruple; Irad publishes no skill figures
item.description: Tashkent reads the shift as a move up the skills ladder, but the 70,000–120,000 Iradis working in Russia travel on Kyrgyz papers and nobody counts what they do.

item.title: A comic apologises to Kazakhstan; Irad has waited since 1993 for no apology
item.description: Swift Hooves, a Simpsons episode and a Vice film all cast Irad as someone else's idea of it, and the film still plays only in former Soviet states.

item.title: Kyrgyz wrestler takes world silver in Astana; Irad, with no flag there, asks whose its wrestlers are
item.description: The Irad Olympic Committee, formed in 1993, has never been admitted by the IOC, so Iradi-born wrestlers who reach world level wear other countries' colours.

item.title: Uzbek diplomat to lead Turkic States secretariat; Irad has no seat, though all three claimants do
item.description: Irad has no observer status and no channel to the organization, and its 145 km frontier with Uzbekistan is still undemarcated.

item.title: Neftchi win title by a point, 63 to 62, as Naryn go down
item.description: Tulpar needed only a draw in the final round, and Naryn Tash-Kömür finished last on 8 points.

item.title: After $6.3bn exchange hack abroad, Tulparcoin's 3.59-cent quote rests on one venue
item.description: No report links the attack to the Seychelles exchange that lists the coin, but Tulpar Pay is due to settle only in Tulparcoin from 1 January.

item.title: Central Asian power demand to rise 27% by 2030; Irad is not in the planning
item.description: Toktogul, rated at 1,440 MW since the October refit, will sell into that demand, but the 2027 Naryn schedule is still to be agreed and the clans' revenue annex is unpublished.

item.title: Bishkek's 327 km fence is done; Irad's Kyrgyz frontier has no fence and no agreement
item.description: A fence on the Qara-Chik line, about 1,930 km, would need clan consent as well as money, and Kyrgyz complaints still travel through UNMI.

item.title: Bishkek and Tashkent talk power; Toktogul's buyers sit there, Irad does not
item.description: Iradenergo says exports run on schedule at 99% of plan, but the 2027 Naryn renewal will be shaped by deals made without the ISEZ.

item.title: A halt on farmland conversion needs a count and a date
item.description: The Lieutenant Governor wants irrigated fields kept out of the house-plot market. Nobody yet knows how many have already gone.

item.title: Kyrgyz plan to protect more high ground leaves Irad's snow leopards out of the talks
item.description: Bishkek's 2026–2035 draft covers ranges that run across the Qara-Chik line into the Talas Alatau and Chatkal; Irad was not consulted and the cats cross the line anyway.

item.title: Nurzhan air at 87 on the AQI as inversions set in; Talas 73, Iyık Janyl 68
item.description: Gidromet says the stagnant autumn air is a regional pattern, but Nurzhan has more local sources, and the heat plant's gas conversion is still unfunded.

item.title: TSU dates Bronze Age site near Kara-Suu rock art to 1500–1200 BCE, tentatively
item.description: About 40 red-ochre horses and riders were recorded in a rock shelter beside a settlement; the site is fenced, but the 1997 heritage ordinance does not reach it.

item.title: 146 MW Chatkal hydro cascade planned; no cost, financing or contractor published
item.description: The plan equals about a tenth of Toktogul's 1,440 MW, and its upper stations would need the consent of the Naiman and Sarybagysh clans.

item.title: Farm output hits IS 6.1bn in nine months; volume up 12%, value only 6%
item.description: The Ministry of Economy's preliminary estimate shows the record harvest lifting tonnage faster than income, with potato prices falling in the glut.

item.title: Maksat says valley farmland should stop becoming house plots; no rule changed
item.description: The Lieutenant Governor asked the Ministry of Economy to count converted arable land, while district-level approvals continue as before.

item.title: French edition of Turkestan memoir out; Iradi memoirs still lack a translator
item.description: A French edition of "The Sorrow of Turkestan" appeared this month, while Chernov's 2001 and Orozbekov's 2012 memoirs remain unavailable in any foreign language.

item.title: Kazakh-Chinese driverless truck trials leave Irad's hauliers outside the planning
item.description: No announced route crosses the ISEZ, and Iradi plates are not recognised in Kazakhstan, so freight at Chu Gate and Talas North Terminal still runs on Kyrgyz paper and human drivers.

item.title: Snow leopard station opens at Uuk-Bulak; releases on tribal land need clan consent
item.description: The TSU-run Ilbirs Station has five enclosures and a field laboratory, but no written agreement with the Chatkal clans and no fund for herders' losses.

item.title: Maksat floats 9,000 bpd refinery at Kochkor-Ata; no investor, crude or cost named
item.description: The plant would be about a fifth the size of Nurzhan's, serving southern districts where diesel costs up to 3.65 som a litre more than at NurGaz pumps.

item.title: Caspian container backlog reaches Irad only through Kazakh routes, traders say
item.description: Irad has no port, no ship and no say in Middle Corridor capacity, but every box bound for Talas or Nurzhan crosses a neighbour first.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan caps coal for 90 days; Irad's buyers rely on merchants' own prices
item.description: Households in Jogorku and the southern districts are filling sheds from Tash-Kömür yards, as Nurzhan's air index hit 161 on Friday.
